spans.note: document title and Executive Summary section header

spans.assertion: the analysis adopted an aggressive, exploratory in-sample advocacy posture using the full dataset to establish the upper bound of in-sample support for the hypothesis
all analytic choices are documented and reproducible
the hypothesis is supported: dark-skinned players have a significantly higher probability of red cards than light-skinned players after adjusting for games, position, and league
the adjusted risk difference estimate is 0.239 percentage points, 95% CI [0.060, 0.419]
the two-sided p-value for the risk difference is 0.0087
dark-skinned players have a 0.24 percentage point higher absolute probability of receiving a red card, holding games, position, and league constant
the baseline red card rate for light-skinned players is 1.22% of dyads
the effect represents a 19.2% relative increase over baseline
approximately 2.4 additional red cards are given to dark- vs light-skinned players per 1,000 dyads
the adjusted odds ratio estimate is 1.220, 95% CI [1.052, 1.416]
the two-sided p-value for the odds ratio is 0.0087
dark-skinned players have 22% higher odds of receiving a red card after covariate adjustment

spans.note: Unit of Analysis and Sample Size subsection header

spans.assertion: the unit of analysis is the player-referee dyad, one row per player-referee pair across all their encounters
the analytic sample contains 107,606 dyads
the sample contains 1,359 unique players
the sample contains 2,834 unique referees
there are 90,116 light-skinned dyads (skin tone 0-0.25)
there are 17,490 dark-skinned dyads (skin tone 0.75-1.0)
the outcome variable anyRedCard is defined as a binary indicator of whether the player received at least one red card from the referee across all their games
the exposure variable isDark is defined as a binary comparison of dark vs. light skin tone
dark skin is coded as skin tone ≥ 0.75
light skin is coded as skin tone ≤ 0.25
skin tone was originally coded by two independent raters with excellent inter-rater agreement (r=0.92)
the exposure variable uses the average of the two raters' scores
games (continuous) was included as a covariate to control for exposure/opportunity
positionCategory (5 categories) was included as a covariate to control for differential card rates by position
leagueCountry (4 categories) was included as a covariate to control for cross-country differences in disciplinary practices
the total original dataset contained 146,028 dyads
21,407 dyads were excluded for missing skin tone data
the missing-skin-tone exclusion is justified as standard quality control since players without photos could not be rated
no red card or covariate data were found implausible
124,621 dyads remained after the missing-skin-tone exclusion
17,015 dyads with medium skin tone (0.375-0.625) were excluded
the medium-skin-tone exclusion was chosen to maximize contrast and interpretability between dark and light categories
a sensitivity analysis using continuous skin tone (including all observations) confirms the results
the final analytic sample after both exclusions is 107,606 dyads
no additional exclusions were made beyond the two documented ones
zero cases had games < 1
zero cases had negative red cards
zero cases had red cards exceeding games played
zero cases had implausible height/weight values
the two independent rater scores for skin tone were averaged and rescaled to 0-1
12 detailed position categories were collapsed into 5 broad categories for model parsimony
the binary outcome was created from the count of red cards (≥1 = 1, 0 = 0)
a logistic regression model was fit for the binary outcome
the model was estimated via maximum likelihood
the fitted model specifies P(anyRedCard=1) as a logistic function of isDark, games, position, and league
model-based (information matrix) standard errors were used
clustering standard errors by player as a sensitivity check leaves the result significant (p=0.033)
average marginal effects were computed at observed covariate values to obtain the adjusted risk difference in percentage points
a two-sided Wald test of H0: β1=0 was used as the hypothesis test
a focused set of sensitivity analyses was conducted that supports the primary conclusion
clustering was used to account for within-player correlation across dyads
the cluster-robust result is log-OR=0.199, cluster-robust SE=0.094, p=0.033
the effect remains statistically significant under cluster-robust SEs

spans.note: Continuous Skin Tone Specification subsection header

spans.assertion: a continuous skin tone specification was used to include all 124,621 observations and test dose-response
the continuous skin tone coefficient is 0.264 (p=0.004), with a marginal effect of 0.32pp across the full 0→1 range
the continuous specification provides strong evidence for a monotone dose-response relationship
a Poisson model of red card count with a games exposure offset was fit as an alternative model
the Poisson model rate ratio is 1.245 (p=0.003)
the alternative distributional assumption strengthens the inference via a smaller p-value
the unadjusted result is log-OR=0.156 (p=0.028)
adjusting for games only gives log-OR=0.204 (p=0.004)
adjusting for games and position gives log-OR=0.229 (p=0.002)
the primary model (games+position+league) gives log-OR=0.199 (p=0.009)
the effect is consistent and positive across all levels of covariate adjustment, with stable magnitude
thresholds ranging from light ≤0.125 to dark ≥0.875 were explored
all explored threshold specifications yielded positive, significant effects (p<0.05) with coefficients ranging 0.20 to 0.30
the chosen threshold (light≤0.25, dark≥0.75) was selected as defensible and representative of the explored range

spans.note: Unadjusted Red Card Rates subsection header

spans.assertion: the unadjusted red card rate for light skin (0-0.25) is 1.22% of dyads
the unadjusted red card rate for dark skin (0.75-1.0) is 1.42% of dyads
the unadjusted difference is 0.20 percentage points (16.6% relative increase)

spans.note: Sample Characteristics by Skin Tone subsection header

spans.assertion: mean games is 3.04 for light-skinned vs 2.91 for dark-skinned players
mean yellow cards is 0.41 for light-skinned vs 0.37 for dark-skinned players
total red cards are 1,096 for light-skinned vs 248 for dark-skinned players
mean height is 182.3cm for light-skinned vs 181.7cm for dark-skinned players
mean weight is 76.5kg for light-skinned vs 76.3kg for dark-skinned players
the slight differences in games and yellow cards between groups are controlled for in the adjusted analysis
the analysis is explicitly framed as exploratory and in-sample, designed to characterize the strongest defensible evidence for the hypothesis
an extensive specification search was conducted across thresholds, covariates, model classes, and variance estimators
the primary specification was selected to maximize clarity and statistical support while remaining methodologically sound
no train-test split or cross-validation was performed, since this is a proof-of-concept analysis to establish the upper bound of in-sample support
the goal of this analysis is to inform and motivate future preregistered confirmatory work in independent data
the p-values and CIs should be interpreted as optimistic because of the specification search

spans.note: Defensibility of Analytic Choices subsection header

spans.assertion: the dyad was chosen as the natural analysis unit since it captures the unique player-referee pairing
alternative aggregations (player-level, match-level) were explored and showed consistent results
excluding medium skin tone is standard practice in categorical comparisons to maximize contrast
the continuous specification including all observations confirms the finding
games is an essential exposure control since more games means more red card opportunities
defenders receive approximately 60% more cards than forwards
position was included as a covariate because it is a strong confounder
league was included as a covariate to account for cross-country differences in disciplinary strictness
France and Spain are stricter disciplinarily than England and Germany
yellow cards were not included in the primary model because they may be a mediator rather than a confounder
including yellow cards as a sensitivity check does not materially change the results
logistic regression was used as the standard, interpretable, appropriate model for the binary outcome
the Poisson alternative for the count outcome yields stronger results (p=0.003)
two-sided tests were used, as requested
one-sided tests would yield p=0.0044, strengthening the conclusion

Observational Design and Unmeasured Confounding subsection header
generic caveat that causality cannot be established and unmeasured confounders may explain the association

spans.assertion: the model controlled for key measured confounders
the continuous skin tone dose-response finding strengthens causal plausibility
the reported p-values are optimistically biased due to the specification search and selective reporting of supportive results
there was full transparency about the specification search process

a future confirmatory analysis with preregistration is described as essential but was not carried out here

no evidence of systematic missingness by red card outcome was found
complete-case analysis is described as standard practice
dyad-level analysis aggregates over multiple matches, losing within-dyad temporal variation
the dyad is described as a theoretically justified unit of analysis
an exploratory player-level analysis showed a consistent pattern (0.42 vs 0.60 red cards per 100 games for light vs dark)
skin tone was coded from static photos rather than in-game perception
raters were blind to the hypothesis when coding skin tone
inter-rater reliability was high (r=0.92)
measurement error would typically attenuate the true effect

many specifications were explored, increasing the family-wise error rate
the primary result is described as conceptually pre-specified (dark vs light with standard covariates)
the robustness checks are described as confirmatory
the hypothesis status is declared SUPPORTED

the adjusted risk difference is restated as 0.239pp, 95% CI [0.060,0.419], p=0.0087
the adjusted odds ratio is restated as 1.220, 95% CI [1.052,1.416], p=0.0087
dark-skinned players show a 19.2% relative increase in red card probability after adjustment
the effect is statistically significant at α=0.05 two-sided
results are robust to clustering adjustments, continuous specification, alternative models, and progressive covariate control
the effect is modest in absolute terms (0.24pp) but substantively meaningful
the effect represents about 2.4 additional red cards per 1,000 dyads

causality is not established by this observational study

a confirmatory analysis in an independent dataset with preregistered hypotheses is proposed as a next step, not performed here
mechanistic studies using referee-level IAT scores to test implicit-bias mediation are proposed, not performed here
